children: reported a marginal rise in its full-year profit on Monday, helped by healthy growth in deposits and lending, although mortgage demand slowed following the government's tax changes.

The country's third-largest lender by market value reported net profit excluding notable items of A$6.99 billion ($4.91 billion) for the year ended September 30, compared with A$6.97 billion reported last year.
That was in line with the Visible Alpha consensus estimate of A$6.99 billion.
Westpac said its deposits and loans grew by 6% and 5%, respectively, during the financial year.
The country's second-largest mortgage lender by loans said Australian housing loans, excluding RAMS, increased by 7%.
Lending to business rose by 12%, and strong credit demand across sectors including energy, infrastructure and resources drove institutional lending 18% higher.
However, the bank saw a 15% decline in average monthly mortgage applications in the fourth quarter, compared with the same period last year.
Housing mortgage and investor credit demand has weakened since the government scrapped tax concessions for property investors earlier in the year.
That has pressured Australia's top four banks, which account for more than 70% of the mortgage market and rely on home lending as a key source of profit.
Westpac declared a final dividend of 77 Australian cents per share, same as last year.

Its core net interest margin, a key measure of profitability, slid 5 basis points from last year to 1.76%, while its common equity tier 1 ratio, a measure of spare cash, slipped 7 basis points to 12.46%.
